**A Dynamic Island for your Android punch-hole camera — running over every app on the phone.**

Not a mock-up and not a wallpaper. Dynamic Camera Punch is a system overlay that turns the camera cutout into a live pill: at rest it is a circle around the hole, indistinguishable from the cutout itself. Something happens, it grows out of the hole to show you; the moment passes, it shrinks back and disappears.

## New in 2.8.0 — a see-through island

### Background opacity, 0 to 100

A slider in the **Island** tab, under **Surface**. At 100 the island is solid; at 0 the surface is gone entirely and only the content is left floating over whatever is behind it. Everything in between is a normal translucent panel.

It multiplies whatever alpha your chosen background colour already has, rather than replacing it — so picking a deliberately translucent colour is not silently forced back to solid by a dial sitting at 100.

### Blur behind

Also under **Surface**, 0–80 dp. A translucent panel over a busy wallpaper is unreadable; a blurred one is not, which is what makes real glass look like glass.

Two honest limits, stated on the card: it needs **Android 12 or later**, and the system switches all window blurs off in battery saver and when "reduce transparency" is on. The app asks the platform whether blurs are enabled and quietly draws flat when they are not, rather than pretending.

### More to change

**Content** — text size (80–130%), artwork size, artwork corner radius, transport button size.

**Media** — show the progress bar, show elapsed and remaining, and a progress style: plain bar or **wave**. The wave animates the played side and resolves into a flat line at the playhead.

**Feel** — haptics on open and hold, switchable.

That is eleven new settings, all saved into presets like the rest.

## Fixed — the transport row

**The row is now always three buttons, in a fixed order.**

A media session declares which transports it supports, and building the row from that declaration seemed reasonable — until the first track of a queue drops "previous", the row becomes two buttons, and everything shifts sideways. That is the "sometimes the forward button is there but the back button is missing" report. A control row that changes shape reads as broken, not as unavailable.

Now the row is fixed at previous / play-pause / next, and the declared actions only decide what is drawn **dimmed**. A session that declares nothing at all — plenty of players never populate the field — is treated as supporting everything, because greying out a control that would have worked is the worse mistake.

Two related fixes: the row is squeezed rather than allowed to overflow the island's padded span, so an outermost button can never be drawn past the window edge and simply not be there; and the expanded height calculation now reads the same dials the drawing does, so a taller header can no longer be clipped by a box that did not grow with it.

**Progress now shows the clock.** Elapsed on the left, remaining on the right as a negative — `1:16` … `-2:16` — the convention every music player uses.

## What it shows

| Source | On the island | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Messages** | The conversation and what was actually said, with the sender's avatar. Tap to open the thread. | Notification access |
| **Media** | The track that is playing, with working previous / play / next and a live progress bar | Notification access |
| **Calls** | The incoming caller, read from the dialer's own notification | Notification access |
| **Timers & alarms** | Live countdown from the clock app | Notification access |
| **Navigation** | Turn-by-turn from the maps app | Notification access |
| **Downloads** | Progress from anything reporting it | Notification access |
| **Charging** | Bolt and battery level the moment you plug in | *nothing* |
| **Battery low** | Level and warning | *nothing* |
| **Ringer** | Silent / vibrate / ring changes | *nothing* |
| **Headphones** | Connect and disconnect | *nothing* |

## How it works

**A system overlay, not a launcher widget.** The island is a `TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY` window owned by a foreground service, so it draws above every app on the device.

**Drawn on a Canvas, not built from widgets.** An overlay window has to be exactly the size of its touchable content, because every pixel it covers is a pixel the app underneath stops receiving touches on. The island changes size constantly, so its window is re-measured on every animation frame — cheap for a custom `View`, ruinous for anything heavier. One interpolator, `cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)`, carries the whole morph.

**The camera never moves.** The window is centre-anchored and the lens is drawn at a fixed offset inside the island, so no state change can slide the hole off the physical sensor.

**Media comes from `MediaSessionManager`, not from the notification.** Media notifications are skipped by the notification reader entirely, so there is exactly one source of truth for what is playing and one place the transport row is built.

**No libraries.** No AndroidX, no Kotlin runtime, no third-party code — the framework `View` and `Canvas` only. A system-wide overlay, a three-tab control panel, an offline support page and a full browser demonstration in 181 KB.

### Permissions

Six, each used by code in the app: `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE` + `…_SPECIAL_USE`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`, `BIND_NOTIFICATION_LISTENER_SERVICE`, plus a `&lt;queries&gt;` declaration (not a permission) so the app picker can list apps with a launcher icon.

**Not requested:** `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, `READ_PHONE_STATE`, and `INTERNET` — the app has never made a network request and cannot. Notifications are read only; nothing is stored or sent anywhere.

## Setup

1. **Display over other apps** — required.
2. **Notification access** — optional but recommended; this is what makes the content real.
3. **Show notifications** — Android requires an ongoing notification for a service that runs indefinitely.

Minimum Android 7.0 (API 24) · targetSdk 34 · about 181 KB on disk · working set 30–45 MB.

---

## Known limitations

- Blur needs Android 12+, and the system disables all window blurs in battery saver or with "reduce transparency" on.
- Some manufacturer skins — notably Xiaomi/MIUI and some Huawei builds — add their own extra "show on top" toggle and aggressively kill background services.
- If your phone's *own* media notification is what you are seeing rather than the island, the **Show only on the island** switch clears the duplicate once the island has shown it.
- This build has not been run on physical hardware, so please open an issue with a screenshot if something looks wrong.
